text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

- Authorities plan to restructure the country's hospitals and remove emergency wards from some of them. This way a number of hospitals will be able to specialise in treating many patients suffering from various long-term illnesses.

- Erik Solheim, leader of the Socialist Left Party, wants parliament to impose restrictions on how big holiday houses are allowed to be. Anyone owning a holiday house larger than 150 square meters must also live there permanently, he suggests. Newspapers have reported that millionaires spend enormous sums of money on buying bigger and bigger weekend houses around the coast of Norway.

- An official was run down when the brakes of a rally car malfunctioned at a race at the weekend. The official was brought to an Oslo hospital in the second accident involving rally racing in Norway for three months.
- Poor ventilation in schools has a negative impact on the concentration of pupils, a study shows. Pupils complain they often get a headache.
- Members of the right-wing extremist groups Viking and White Aryan Terror claim to have 30 fire arms hidden in Oslo and two other areas.
- Hydro Aluminum is preparing acquisitions of companies in China together with its partner Temasek in Singapore.

- Administrators of Noka Securities now ask all clients of the bankrupted brokerhouse to check if their own accounts match those of Noka. A former Noka manager was remanded in custody for a week on Saturday on suspicion of inflicting losses on the brokerhouse and of forging documents.
- Two more holiday houses on the coast are for sale and the price is expected to be at least 10 million crowns each. The question is how this phenomenon, which many call madness, is going to end.
- Norsk Hydro may have lost several million crowns after the mafia allegedly pushed the company out of Ukraine, where it was involved in building an export terminal for fertilisers.
- State-owned oil companyt Statoil is investing in Brasil in cooperation with the state-owned oil giant Petrobras.
